data.name: BATTLETECH
data.detailed_description:
From original BATTLETECH/MechWarrior creator Jordan Weisman and the developers of the award-winning Shadowrun Returns series comes the next-generation of turn-based tactical 'Mech combat.

The year is 3025 and the galaxy is trapped in a cycle of perpetual war, fought by noble houses with enormous, mechanized combat vehicles called BattleMechs. Take command of your own mercenary outfit of 'Mechs and the MechWarriors that pilot them, struggling to stay afloat as you find yourself drawn into a brutal interstellar civil war. Upgrade your starfaring base of operations, negotiate mercenary contracts with feudal lords, repair and maintain your stable of aging BattleMechs, and execute devastating combat tactics to defeat your enemies on the battlefield.

COMMAND A SQUAD OF 'MECHS IN TURN-BASED COMBAT

Deploy over 30 BattleMechs in a wide variety of combinations. Use terrain, positioning, weapon selection and special abilities to outmaneuver and outplay your opponents.

MANAGE YOUR MERCENARY COMPANY

Recruit, customize, and develop unique MechWarriors. Improve and customize your dropship. As a Mercenary, travel a wide stretch of space, taking missions and managing your reputation with a variety of noble houses and local factions.

TAKE PART IN A DESPERATE CIVIL WAR

Immerse yourself in the story of a violently deposed ruler, waging a brutal war to take back her throne with the support of your ragtag mercenary company.

CUSTOMIZE YOUR 'MECHS

Use your MechLab to maintain and upgrade your units, replacing damaged weapon systems with battlefield salvage taken from fallen foes.

PVP MULTIPLAYER & SKIRMISH MODE

Customize a Lance of 'Mechs and MechWarriors to go head-to-head with your friends, compete against opponents online, or jump into single-player skirmish mode to test your strategies against the AI.

reviews.review:
This game has been a random pick which I do not regret in the slightest.

Despite being released in 2018, it still has a lot to offer for an aspiring strategist.

You manage a mercenary company in two of the available three modes of play. The last one being a quick skirmish against AI or another fellow strategist. I didn't try the multiplayer. You need a Paradox account and I assume there won't be many people sticking around in the lobby, even if there is still support after 8 years.

I know next to nothing about the BattleTech franchise. I can't say if the game follows this ruleset or that ruleset, if the units are balanced or not. As an example, I read somewhere that the laser weapons got nerfed too much but I have no reference to compare to and I'm not going to look for one. I simply take what's available and try to make the best out of it.

The two other modes are a campaign which is also a tutorial at the beginning and you follow the Arano Restoration storyline. Besides the Mechs, you also got a ship to travel between planets. You are free to choose where to go and as far as I know there is no real time limit in the campaign mode. It is your decision if you want to do the story missions or not. After you finish the campaign, you can continue playing, which is great if you want to collect more weapons and more mechs.

The last mode is called Career. At the beginning, you select the game parameters and there are quite a few of them. This mode allows you to test your skills at management and tactical combat. It is basically the same mode as the campaign but without the story missions. In addition, there is a 1200 in-game days to reach the best score you can. The game parameters introduce a score modifier which can be maxed at 1.00. This modifier is then multiplied by your score. Obviously, if you want the best multiplier, you have to make some choices, which make the game harder for you. Less payout, less rewards, harder fights, lethal pilot injuries and so on.

You have unlimited space in your storage but only six mechs are battle ready in your bay. You will also upgrade your ship and buy two more bays for 18 mechs if you so desire. Other ship upgrade are faster travel between planets, living space for more pilots, faster mech repairs/customizations, etc. Decisions, decisions, decisions.

Mechs fall into four categories: light, medium, heavy and assault. There are also quite a many mechs to choose from. You start with a random group from the starting pool (or you can choose default [in career]). Mechs have characteristics like: tonnage, how many weapons and what type they can mount, movement efficiency, heat efficiency (yep, firing weapons generates heat, overheating a mech is not really recommended). As for weapons, there are ballistic cannons, rockets, lasers and support weapons (really short-range). Your job is to figure out what weapon combination is the best for given mech.

And which combination of mechs is the best in your situation. And which mechs are better than other mechs :)

The simplest rule is: the heavier the mech, the better. More weapons, more armor. Interestingly, some medium mechs are worse than light mechs. Heavies worse than mediums. You get the drift.

To make it more interesting, there are also rare mech variants and better weapon versions (+ version, ++ and +++ versions). There is always something to hunt for. After each battle you collect salvage in form of mech parts and weapons/equipment. Equipment is a special mech part, which gives you some advantage in the combat. Like better radar range, better melee attack (yes, mechs can go melee too!), jumpjets, heatsinks, cockpit protection and so on. You can influence to certain extent what salvage you get. If you completely destroy opposing mech, you get only one part, if you headshot the pilot though, you get three parts. By default, three parts are needed to assemble a brand new mech. Headshots are pretty unlikely though unless you know what you are doing.

Pilots get experience after each battle too. And there are four skill trees to upgrade their abilities.

Missions take place in different environments, which impacts the heat economy the most. Freezing planet vs. scorching hot. Can make some of your hotter mechs quite unusable.

Each planet has a store and in some cases the Black Market. That's the place to buy the  good stuff for $$$$.

Deciding where to go, what missions to take, damage mitigation that's all part of the decision making in this game. The mech repairs and/or pilot injuries can be a major inconvenience. Mechs can't be repaired in parallel. If your mechs get damaged a lot and often, you can forget reaching a good score in career. Spending 20 days repairing one mech is pretty bad. Unless you combine it with the space travel. Spending 15+ days travelling between planets is normal.

You also need to manage your reputation with 8 major factions. If you go too low, you won't be able to take any contracts (missions) from them. Also, a faction won't give you a higher tier contract if you don't have good reputation with them. As you can guess, each contract is issued by one faction against another faction. Reputation for the issuer goes up (if the mission is a success) and the target's reputation goes down.

It may sound complex but it isn't. Too much. There are much more complex games out there.

I like the freedom and options the game gives you. Go anywhere, choose any mechs, any loadout, do any mission available and if you get your ass kicked, well, that's on you :)
